methodological_rigor.justification: Dual-center retrospective cohort with 109 patients (55 HIPEC, 54 control). Well-balanced baseline characteristics (SMD <0.2), multivariate Cox regression with appropriate proportional hazards assumption testing. Follows STROBE guidelines. Key limitations: retrospective non-randomized design susceptible to selection bias despite balanced variables; univariate analysis suggests modest statistical power; no propensity score matching due to small sample size acknowledged.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort study (LoE 2b) demonstrating novel modified HIPEC protocol combined with minimally invasive LPD. Direct clinical relevance to pancreatic cancer surgical management. Shows 4-month median OS improvement (27 vs 23 months) and reduced locoregional recurrence (14.6% vs 31.5%). Clinically meaningful in context of aggressive disease, though marginal statistical significance (P=0.045) acknowledged.

reporting_quality.justification: Explicit STROBE compliance stated; comprehensive reporting of patient selection, study design, statistical methods, and limitations. Detailed complication classification using Clavien-Dindo and ISGPS criteria. Clear outcome definitions including recurrence patterns. However, no statement of data availability, code sharing, or repository deposition. Methods partially reproducible but require institutional protocols and access to patient cohort.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel multi-stage perioperative HIPEC protocol combining intraoperative hyperthermic saline, delayed postoperative gemcitabine (POD2), and final saline lavage (POD4). First published evaluation of this hybrid HIPEC-EPIC approach combined with laparoscopic (not open) pancreaticoduodenectomy. Conceptual innovation in timing and staging distinguishes from conventional single-stage intraoperative HIPEC literature.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript with clear clinical problem statement, detailed technical descriptions of surgical technique and HIPEC protocol with temperature/perfusion parameters, comprehensive results tables with Kaplan-Meier curves, and thorough discussion of limitations including sample size constraints and follow-up discrepancies. Minor issues: marginal P-value discussion could be more prominent earlier.

key_strengths: Dual-center study with well-balanced baseline characteristics (SMD <0.2) across demographic and oncologic variables reducing apparent selection bias
Novel multi-stage perioperative HIPEC protocol rationally designed to integrate hyperthermic lavage with delayed gemcitabine administration for safety and efficacy
Comprehensive complication reporting per standardized Clavien-Dindo and ISGPS criteria showing no increase in severe morbidity despite complex combined procedure
Demonstrates significant reduction in locoregional recurrence (14.6% vs 31.5%, P=0.035) supporting mechanistic hypothesis for locoregional therapy
Multivariate Cox analysis with proportional hazards assumption testing; identifies LPD+HIPEC as independent prognostic factor (HR 0.58, P=0.038)
key_concerns: Marginal primary outcome significance (P=0.045) with acknowledged limited statistical power from modest sample size; authors note 4-month median OS improvement but confidence intervals overlap at extremes

Retrospective non-randomized design with shared decision-making allocation potentially creating unmeasured bias despite balanced observed covariates; acknowledged limitation that propensity score matching infeasible due to sample size
Discrepancy in median follow-up duration between groups (18 vs 12 months) may underestimate late recurrences in control arm and create differential ascertainment bias

Two in-hospital deaths in HIPEC group versus zero in control group (not statistically significant but clinically concerning) suggesting careful patient selection needed; unclear if analysis adjusted for patient fitness beyond ECOG status
No data sharing statement, code availability, or method for external validation; results from high-volume centers (>2000 LPDs since 2013) may not generalize to lower-volume institutions
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically competent dual-center study with novel protocol innovation but borderline statistical significance and limited sample size restrict tier placement. Appropriate for Tier 3 (4-9.9 JIF) with major revisions addressing statistical power calculations, patient selection criteria, and equal follow-up protocols before publication.
